text: At two hundred and thirty kilometres an hour, water hits like concrete.
If one wingtip or engine digs in first, a plane can cartwheel, and break apart.
So a water landing needs wings perfectly level, the nose slightly up, and the slowest, gentlest sink possible.
In two thousand nine, with both engines gone, Captain Sullenberger brought an Airbus down on the Hudson River.
It floated. Passengers stood on the wings until the ferries came.
All one hundred and fifty-five survived. Full video on my channel.
